Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 109, verses 1–6:

(p-701) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surah al-Kafirun

It is Meccan by consensus (ijma').

The Exalted and Majestic One said:

﴿Say: O disbelievers!﴾ ﴿I do not worship what you worship.﴾ ﴿Nor do you worship what I worship.﴾ ﴿Nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped.﴾ ﴿Nor do you worship what I worship.﴾ ﴿For you is your religion, and for me is my religion.﴾

Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Ibn Mas'ud read: "Say to those who disbelieve (qul lilladhina kafaru)."

It is narrated concerning the occasion of revelation of this surah, from Ibn 'Abbas and others, that a group of the most stubborn and leading men of Quraysh said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Leave what you are upon, and we will make you wealthy, marry you to whichever of our noble women you wish, and make you king over us. And if you do not do this, then worship our gods, and we will worship your God, so that we share in it. Wherever the good lies, we will have obtained it together." This is the meaning of their words and the wording of their speech, though the narrators differ in addition and omission. It is also narrated that this group mentioned were: al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, al-'As ibn Wa'il, al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib, Umayya ibn Khalaf, Ubayy ibn Khalaf, Abu Jahl, the two sons of al-Hajjaj, and their peers who had not yet embraced Islam. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had with them various encounters on these matters, and the surah was revealed during one of them, concerning their saying: "Come, let us share in the worship of your God and our gods." It is also narrated that they said: "Worship our god for a year, and we will worship your God for a year." So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, informed them of His command that he does not worship what they worship, and that they are not worshippers of what he worships. Since his saying "I do not worship" could be understood to mean "now" while leaving the future open, awaiting what his worship might become, the clarification came with His saying: ﴿Nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped﴾, meaning never and as long as I live. Then came His saying: ﴿Nor do you worship what I worship﴾, as a decisive statement upon them that they will never believe in Him, like one who has uncovered the unseen. This is like what was said to Noah, peace be upon him: ﴿that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed﴾ [Hud: 36]. Indeed, this has two meanings, and the people of Noah were blinded by this. This is the meaning of the repetition in the surah, and it is of eloquent excellence, and is not mere repetition; rather it contains what I have mentioned along with emphasis and conveyance. He increased the matter in clarity and in disassociation from them with His saying: ﴿For you is your religion, and for me is my religion﴾. In connection with this matter, which Quraysh put forward, there was also revealed: ﴿Say: Do you order me to worship other than Allah, O ignorant ones?﴾ [Az-Zumar: 64].

Abu 'Amr read: "wa-liya dini" with the yā' of "liya" silent, while the rest read it with a fatha, with variation transmitted from each of them; both readings are good. Some read "'abid" and "'abidun" with imala, and others with fatha; both are also good. The Seven did not differ over the deletion of the yā' in "dini," while Sallam and Ya'qub affirmed it both in pausal and continuous recitation. Some scholars said: in these expressions there is a certain truce (muhadana), and it is abrogated by the verse of fighting (ayat al-qital).

The tafsir of Surah [al-Kafirun] is complete, and all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
